profile.facility_type_note: Part of Digital Realty's Silicon Valley (Santa Clara/San Jose area) data center campus, one of the company's largest US clusters. Two facilities in this group carry independent historic significance: 360 Spear Street and 365 Main Street in San Francisco are separate, well known carrier hotel buildings; 365 Main Street was the site of a widely covered July 2007 power outage that took down major web services including Craigslist and other sites hosted there, later becoming a Digital Realty/Digital Realty-heritage asset. SJC10 is documented at 1100 Space Park Drive per Digital Realty's own site.

reading.body:
Digital Realty's Santa Clara facility SJC16 spans 42,500 square feet with N+2 cooling redundancy, but the operator publishes no power capacity figure for this building.

The absence of disclosed megawatt capacity at a major carrier-class facility in Silicon Valley reflects a broader opacity in data center infrastructure disclosure. Digital Realty operates one of the largest US data center clusters in the Santa Clara and San Jose area, yet granular power specifications remain unpublished even for individual named buildings within that footprint. This contrasts sharply with the visibility into cooling architecture, which the operator does advertise as a competitive feature.

For tracking AI's infrastructure constraints, missing power data creates a real gap. Cooling redundancy describes resilience but not demand. A 42,500 square foot facility in a region where compute density has risen sharply could represent anywhere from tens to hundreds of megawatts depending on workload and hardware vintage. Without published figures, researchers assessing whether grid capacity or building availability is the binding constraint on regional AI scaling must rely on older benchmarks or inference from aggregate corporate disclosures.

The Santa Clara campus itself carries historical weight in data center culture through its connection to 365 Main Street, where a 2007 outage took down major web services. That incident, now part of Digital Realty's own heritage narrative, underscores how power and cooling failures at individual buildings have reshaped industry thinking about redundancy. SJC16's N+2 cooling posture reflects that learned dependency, though it does not address electrical supply risk upstream of the facility itself.
